thread.title: Stocks Surge, Dow Jones Stock Jumps Into Buy Zone | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Surge, Dow Jones Stock Jumps Into Buy Zone | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks rallied, but came off early highs Wednesday, as Boeing stock and Apple earnings drove the Dow Jones industrials nearer to the 25,000 mark. Markets were also tuned to events in Washington, with U.S.-China trade talks underway and a Federal Reserve policy announcement due this afternoon.
X Apple ( AAPL ) stock vaulted after positive earnings relieved markets late Tuesday . Boeing ( BA ) stock thundered higher on the heels of its fourth-quarter result s. Chip stocks were split: Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) soared on earnings , Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) spiked on takeover news , while MKS Instruments ( MKSI ) took a hard hit on earnings results. Other stocks trading lower on earnings news included Amgen ( AMGN ), Illumina ( ILMN ), Align Technologies ( ALGN ) and Juniper Networks ( JNPR ).
The Dow Jones industrial average leapt 1.1% at the starting bell. The Nasdaq Composite swung 1% higher, while the S&P 500 managed a 0.6% gain.
Boeing and Apple ran at the head of the Dow. Apple led the Nasdaq 100. AMD jumped highest on the S&P 500, with Stryker ( SYK ), Anthem ( ANTM ) and Boeing stock not far behind.

Please contact customer service CLOSE January Hiring Tops Estimates; GDP Data Delayed U.S. non-farm employers added 213,000 workers in January, according to the National Employment Report from ADP. That was down from 271,000 new hires in December, but well above consensus forecasts for a dip to 174,000, as holiday season gigs came to an end. The Labor Department is scheduled to report its December payrolls report on Friday.
The release of fourth-quarter GDP growth estimates scheduled for release from the Commerce Department early Wednesday reportedly was delayed by the federal government shutdown. Federal offices and operations restarted Monday. No firm date has yet been set for the fourth-quarter GDP release.
Stock Futures: Dow Jones Eyes 25,000 The Dow Jones industrial average muscled out an advance on Tuesday, as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both lost ground. All three indexes are holding support above their 50-day lines, a technical positive for the market and its confirmed uptrend. The Dow's move also maintained its holding pattern, just below its 200-day moving average — which is a fraction below the 25,000 mark. The Dow Jones industrials have not closed above the 25,000 level since early December.
For more detailed market analysis, read the Big Picture .
Apple Retakes, Fight To Hold Support Apple stock popped 6.8% in early action, then pared back to a 3.7% gain. Apple earnings and revenue , reported late Tuesday, narrowly beat reduced targets for its fiscal first quarter. Management also trimmed its second-quarter revenue outlook to below analyst targets. Apple shares on Wednesday traded up almost 14% from an early January low, retaking their 10-week moving average. The stock has not closed above its 10-week line since October.
Boeing Stock: Breakout Dow Jones peer Boeing jetted more than 6% higher after reporting its fourth-quarter results. A 14% rise in earnings surprised analyst views for a 5% decline. Revenue rose more than 14%, to $28.3 billion, vs. forecasts for $26.8 billion. The commercial segment's operating margin surged to 15.6%, from 11.6%, and management hoisted its full-year earnings and revenue guidance to above analyst targets .
The gap up gain sent Boeing stock past a 367.42 buy point in a first-stage cup-with-handle base. The stock remained in its buy range .
Federal Reserve Policy, Comments The Federal Reserve ends the two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee with a rate policy announcement at 2 p.m. ET, followed by a press briefing with Fed Chair Jerome Powell at 2:30 p.m. Investors expect no change in rate policy, but Powell's comments on reductions in Fed bond holdings amassed during quantitative easing stimulus efforts, and on the policy outlook, will be carefully parsed.
U.S.-China Trade Talks; China, Japan Markets U.S.-China trade talks get underway in Washington where a delegation led by Chinese Vice Premier Liu He and central bank Governor Yi Gang began meeting with U.S. negotiators under Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer. China reportedly has accelerated plans to update its foreign investment law in order to eliminate forced technology transfers and to better defend intellectual property rights, key demands by the U.S.
President Trump and Lighthizer's team have come under increasing pressure from agriculture, auto makers and oil producers to press for a deal, according to the Wall Street Journal. The talks are set to wrap up on Thursday. Tariffs on China-made imports worth $200 billion per year are set to increase from 10% to 25% on March 2.
Meanwhile, China's markets were mixed Wednesday, as new data reinforced concerns of economic slowing and as the market prepares for its week-long Lunar New Year Holiday next week. China's markets typically decline in the week preceding the holiday, as investors draw cash from investing accounts. The Shanghai Composite fell 0.7%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng climbed 0.4%.
In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 dropped 0.5% as investors looked toward Wednesday's policy announcement from the U.S. Federal Reserve, and awaited any signs of mood change on the U.S.-China trade front.
Chip Stocks: AMD Earnings, Intel's Mellanox Bid Chip stocks were in brisk motion early Wednesday. AMD raced ahead 11% following its earnings report. Mellanox Technologies rolled up more than 6% on reports that Intel ( INTC ) had bid more than $5.5 billion to acquire the Israel-based chipmaker. Intel dipped 0.1%. MKS Instruments shed its premarket loss and rose nearly 4% after solid fourth-quarter results, but on weak first-quarter guidance.
Chip heavyweight Broadcom ( AVGO ) halved its early 1.5% advance. The stock is rising toward the top of a buy range above an early entry at 261.59. That aggressive buy point is in a 13-month saucer base. The base also presents a more conservative buy point at 285.78. The stock on Wednesday traded less than 6% below that buy point.
Oil Prices Top $54 Markets will be keeping an eye on oil prices, which jumped 2% on Tuesday and were rising once more early Wednesday. Concerns over U.S. sanctions against Venezuela's Petróleos de Venezuela helped drive the increase. West Texas Intermediate gained 1.4% to just above $54 a barrel. WTI has traded in the $50-$54 range for the past 2-1/2 weeks. A move above or below that range could signal a trend change. Europe's Brent crude benchmark rose 1% to just below $62 a barrel.
